author: reek
body: The schematic data model for Codex Circuits. Every object that can appear on a schematic sheet lives here: wires, junctions, labels, power symbols, component instances, and hierarchical sheet references. Coordinates are in nanometres to match the rest of the EDA suite.

author: reek
body: A wire segment connects two points on the schematic grid. Every segment belongs to exactly one net. A junction marks an explicit connection where three or more wire segments meet at a point.

author: reek
body: A bus entry connects a single net to a bus. The bus carries a group of nets; the entry peels off one named net from the named bus.

author: reek
body: A no-connect marker tells ERC that an unconnected pin is intentional.

author: reek
body: Power symbols inject a named power net onto the schematic. The symbol type controls the graphical rendering.

author: reek
body: Labels assign net names to wires. A NetLabel is local to one sheet. A GlobalLabel is visible across the entire hierarchy. A HierarchicalLabel connects a net to a parent sheet through a hierarchical pin.

author: reek
body: A placed instance of a component on the schematic. The ref is the reference designator (R1, U3, etc). Rotation is in degrees. Mirror is 1 for mirrored, 0 for normal. Unit selects which unit of a multi-unit component this instance represents.

author: reek
body: A sheet is one page of the schematic. A design can contain multiple sheets arranged in a hierarchy. Sub-sheets are referenced by SubSheetRef records that carry position and size for the sheet box drawn on the parent sheet.
